notes.title: Art and Prototype
notes.content:
Hello Friends! 👋 
Welcome to our journey of discovering [i]Dragon Lands[/i]!

Today, I’d love to continue our discussion on the origins of Dragon Lands by diving into the [b]art style[/b] and [b]prototype[/b] phase.

[h3]ART STYLE[/h3]
This was the most challenging part for me. As a software engineer without an artistic background, finding the right style took a lot of time.
At first, I searched for an art style that I personally liked. My main inspirations were [i]Zelda [/i]and [i]Forager[/i], but I struggled to achieve a similar look. 
After weeks of research and experimentation, I finally found the perfect fit: [b]cute pixel art[/b]!

Here’s an early art prototype made in [i]Unreal Engine 5[/i]! I experimented with shadows, brightness, color palettes, outline colors, and pixel sizes to achieve the look I envisioned

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45468992/b27fbf644897e5e2e65455976415324dfdff4987.png[/img]

After many iterations, and even an engine switch, this is what we achieved. The technique used renders the game in low-resolution texture, then upscales it without anti-aliasing, using an orthographic camera.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45468992/ca2e8df0490c994eead16c1e06fb8086a3973632.gif[/img]


[h3]GAME DESIGN[/h3]
I built several prototypes to test mechanics, replayability, and overall fun. At this stage, visuals weren’t the focus (I kept everything simple, with basic blocks and sprites).

This was one of the last prototypes I made, where I tested the core gameplay loop: gathering resources, crafting items, collecting dragons, and automating the farm process.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45468992/59169f0978b93ca4ddd8f7ad50e2aa78cb4cc067.gif[/img]

If you have any questions, feel free to ask me on [url=https://discord.gg/ep4t93D93p]Discord[/url], I’d be happy to chat! :D


Thanks, and stay tuned for more updates!
[i]Giuseppe[/i]

notes.title: Dragon Lands Origins
notes.content:
Hello Friends! 

Welcome to our first update about [i]Dragon Lands[/i]!

The game isn't out yet, but we’re very excited to share details, screenshots, and progress with you. For this first update, I’d like to talk a bit about Dragon Lands' origins.

[h3]THE IDEA[/h3]
After releasing my first game (Core Devourer), I went through months of struggling with inspiration. During that time, I threw myself into various activities like marketing research, studying of art styles that I liked,  prototyping a fighting party games for my friends ([i]which was ultimately scrapped :D[/i]), and, of course, playing other games. 

I spent countless hours playing Forager, Outpath an Nova Lands! Then I've approched incremental games like Gnorp, To The Core and Nodebuster.

Through it all, my thoughts kept circling back to creating an idle incremental game, that could offer a similarly engaging experience.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45468992/b3ba88179dfc44a438834194229d9e00b24a2f3a.gif[/img]

[h3]CONCEPT[/h3]
I had two main goals:
[list]
[*]To create a relaxing game with simple yet deep mechanics and game systems. In other words, a chill game that can be played while watching or doing something else on a second monitor ([i]like I often do[/i]).
[*]Who hasn’t dreamed of owning and collecting dragons?
[/list]
With these pillars in mind, I designed the first prototypes of Dragon Lands with the help of my girlfriend (which is not forced at all :D)!

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45468992/ca2e8df0490c994eead16c1e06fb8086a3973632.gif[/img]

I hope you’ll enjoy the game as much as I do while developing it!

Thanks, and stay tuned for more updates :D

[i]Giuseppe[/i]
